title: Sherpa UI Composition Map
description: The NEUTRAL PIVOT (intermediate representation) between a Figma frame and a Sherpa-UI code view. A composition-map is the single serialisable source of truth for a persisted composition: it can be COMPILED into a Figma frame (instances + overrides + mode pins) AND into a code view-definition (schema/view-definition.schema.json) → renderView() → DOM/HTML, and it is what the Figma EXTRACTOR emits when it reads a frame back out. Neither the Figma spec nor the code view-definition is derived from the other — both are projections OF this map (see docs/COMPOSITION-MAP.md). Every node carries a `role` discriminator that tells each compiler how to treat it. Contract-tier metadata (a component TYPE's attributes/events/slots) is NOT here — that lives in JSDoc and is referenced by `component`; this map is the INSTANCE tier (a specific placement).

map.description: Optional human label for this composition (e.g. 'donut-dashboard').

root.description: The id of the top node of the composition tree. Must be a key in `nodes`.

source.description: Provenance — where this map was extracted from / last compiled to. Advisory; used for round-trip identity checks and re-compilation, never for rendering.

figmaFileKey.description: Figma file key the map was extracted from / targets.

figmaNodeId.description: The Figma node id of `root` (e.g. '518:68914'), for re-compile-in-place.

extractedAt.description: ISO timestamp of extraction (stamped by the extractor, not the schema).

state.description: Free-form state blob, projected verbatim into the code view-definition's `state`. Figma has no runtime state, so this is CODE-ONLY metadata carried through the pivot (Figma prototyping wiring projects from `wires`, below, not from here). `{ "$state": "/ptr" }` bindings in node props/data resolve against this.

nodes.description: Flat registry of every node in the composition, keyed by id. Identity is separate from layout: a node is placed by being referenced in a parent's `children` (default slot) or `slots` (named slot). Mirrors the code view-definition's `elements` map so the code projection is near-mechanical.

nodeId.description: Node id — a stable handle for references, overrides, and round-trip diffing.

node.description: One placed node. The `role` discriminator governs how each compiler projects it. See docs/COMPOSITION-MAP.md §Roles.

role.description: How the CODE projection treats this node (the primary direction is Figma→code — see docs/COMPOSITION-MAP.md §Direction). `component` = a real sherpa-* component the designer placed as a design-system instance → code emits a <sherpa-*> custom element. `pseudo` = LOOSE, editable layers in Figma (deliberately NOT componentised there, so designers reshape them in place) that in CODE become a REAL reusable component/module (arc/bar/gridlines/spline) — the inversion: raw in Figma, DRY in code. `container` = a layout frame (Figma auto-layout/GRID; code layout element or div). `raw` = one-off geometry with no reusable nature; a literal primitive on both sides (Figma vector; code `codeHint` literal). Default Figma posture for ALL roles: DON'T componentise in Figma unless explicitly asked — keep the design designer-friendly; reuse lives in the code projection.

type.description: For role=component: the literal custom-element tag ('sherpa-metric') the code projection emits (the Figma side is a placed design-system instance the designer already made). For role=pseudo: the reusable code module's kind ('chart-arc', 'chart-bar', 'chart-gridlines') the code projection maps to a reusable component/module + its `codeHint` renderer — the Figma side is loose editable layers, not a component. Omitted for container/raw.

props.description: Instance-level attribute values. Keys are literal attribute names (data-* public API; native attrs un-prefixed). The Figma projection maps each to a variant/boolean-prop/text-prop/instance-override per the component's @figma projection rule (see docs); the code projection sets them as attributes. Values: string|number → set; true → boolean/present; false|null → omitted; { "$state": "/ptr" } → code-only state binding (ignored by the Figma projection).

data.description: populate() payload for the CODE projection (array | keyed object | HTML string | { $state } | { src }). The Figma projection does not execute populate(); it may use `data` to stamp representative content into the instance (e.g. legend item labels) but treats it as advisory. Same shape as view-definition `data`.

layout.description: Present mainly on role=container (and any node that owns auto-layout in Figma). The neutral layout description both compilers read: Figma → auto-layout/GRID props; code → CSS grid/flex on the layout element. See §Layout.

figma.description: FIGMA-ONLY metadata that has no code equivalent (mode pins, bound-variable names, paint-style ids, node id for in-place recompile). The code projection ignores this entirely. This is the map's half of the 'each side keeps a private extension' rule — the Figma spec is generated from it.

codeHint.description: CODE-ONLY render recipe for role=pseudo and role=raw. For role=pseudo it names the reusable code module + its parameters ('svg-arc' with {startAngle,endAngle,innerRadius}) — the code projection emits a call to that reusable component/module (this is the DRY-in-code side of the inversion), NOT a per-node copy. For role=raw it's a one-off literal ('svg-path' with a `d`). The Figma projection ignores this (the Figma side of a pseudo is loose editable layers).

slots.description: Named-slot fills: slot name → node id (or array of ids). The parent owns the slot assignment. Figma → append into the instance's SLOT; code → child.slot = name.

children.description: Ordered ids placed in this node's DEFAULT slot (Figma: the instance's/frame's normal-flow children; code: default-slot content).

wires.description: Behavioural wiring, projected BOTH ways: code → view-definition `writes` (event → $state pointer); Figma → a prototype reaction stub (the @fires event → a documented interaction). The event names are the component's real @fires events (validated against the contract). See §Prototyping.

layout.description: Neutral layout description. Deliberately small and mappable to BOTH Figma auto-layout/GRID and CSS. Not a full style system — presentation is tokens/CSS on the code side and bound variables on the Figma side; this is only structural layout.

cols.description: grid only: column count (Figma gridColumnCount ↔ grid-template-columns track count).

colSizes.description: grid column tracks (Figma gridColumnSizes ↔ CSS grid-template-columns).

gap.description: Item spacing — a token name ('space/gap-sm') or px. Figma itemSpacing (bound) ↔ CSS gap.

positioning.description: STRUCTURAL positioning of THIS node within its parent. 'flow' = normal auto-layout/flex flow (default). 'absolute' = an OVERLAY mark that fills its parent independently of flow — chart gridlines and vector marks that layer inside a plot area. Figma layoutPositioning='ABSOLUTE' ↔ code position:absolute inset:0 on an SVG/mark layer over a position:relative parent. This is structural (both worlds need it for charts to round-trip), NOT presentation — hence it lives in the neutral map, not the Figma-only hints.

constraints.description: For positioning='absolute' overlays: how the mark scales with its parent. Figma {horizontal,vertical} STRETCH/SCALE ↔ code SVG sizing (width/height 100% or preserveAspectRatio). 'stretch' = fill the axis (gridlines); 'scale' = scale proportionally (vector marks).

track.description: One grid track. Figma {type:'HUG'|'FIXED'|'FLEX', value} ↔ CSS auto / <px> / <n>fr.

value.description: px for fixed; fr ratio for flex; ignored for hug.

span.description: Optional: track span for a child placed here (Figma gridColumnSpan/RowSpan).

figmaHints.description: Figma-only projection metadata. Generated by the extractor from a live node; consumed by the map→figma compiler. Ignored by the code projection.

nodeId.description: The live Figma node id for compile-in-place / round-trip diffing.

componentKey.description: The component main's key (stable across sessions, unlike nodeId), for resolving the instance to swap in.

modePins.description: explicitVariableModes to pin on the instance (e.g. a Data Viz Sets ramp mode, a Snapping mode, a Status extension). The chart series-colour + status-override contracts ride here.

styleRef.description: Paint-style bindings for pseudo/raw marks that carry style via Figma paint styles rather than component API (e.g. donut segment Categorical Transparent/N fill + Solid/N stroke). The extractor records style ids/names; the compiler re-applies them.

boundVars.description: Bound-variable names by property (e.g. { strokeWeight: 'border/width/base', cornerRadius: 'border/rounding/base' }). For nodes styled by variable binds rather than component API.

codeHint.description: Code inlining recipe for pseudo/raw nodes. `kind` selects a known primitive renderer; `params` parameterises it. The map→view-def compiler emits the corresponding SVG/DOM instead of a custom element.

kind.description: Primitive renderer id — an OPEN registry (free string, deliberately NOT a closed enum): a new mark type is a renderer addition in the code projection, not a schema change. docs/COMPOSITION-MAP.md is the registry of record. Seeded set (transcribed from the charts already built imperatively): 'svg-arc' (donut/gauge segment — params {startAngle,endAngle,innerRadius}), 'svg-trapezoid' (area band), 'svg-polyline' (line), 'svg-rect' (bar — params {valuePct}), 'grid-lines' (chart gridlines — params {count,axis}), 'svg-path' (raw literal — params {d}), 'html' (literal markup — params {markup}). An unknown kind is a validator WARNING (missing renderer), consistent with the warn-don't-block drift policy — never a hard schema error.

params.description: Renderer parameters. e.g. svg-arc: { startAngle, endAngle, innerRadius }; svg-path: { d }; svg-rect: { valuePct }. Style comes from figma.styleRef mapped to CSS classes/vars on the code side.

wire.description: One behavioural wire. Projects to code view-definition `writes` and to a Figma prototype interaction stub.

on.description: Event name — a real @fires event of this component (validated against the contract; drift → warn).

to.description: JSON Pointer into `state` to write on the event (code projection).

value.description: What to write — a '$detail…' path from the event detail. Omit to write the whole detail.

$state.description: JSON Pointer (RFC 6901) into the map `state` blob. Code-only.

src.description: URL to fetch as JSON, then hand to populate(). Code-only.
